subject.title: Exec approvals: make the "Exec approval: Allowed/Denied" outcome echo configurable (edit-only / suppress)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a shared approval-outcome setting now with compatibility-default message delivery and optional suppression, while treating prompt update as a separate capability-backed follow-up?
rationale: This adds a user-facing configuration surface across shared exec/plugin approval delivery; the repository policy requires maintainers to choose the permanent contract rather than let a narrow channel symptom define it.

options.title: Sponsor message and suppression now
options.body: Accept a shared message|none contract with message as the upgrade-safe default, then track update mode separately behind generic delivery identifiers and channel edit capability.

options.title: Design update semantics first
options.body: Pause the narrow setting until the approval lifecycle can reliably associate every delivery with an editable prompt across supported channels.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Decline a new configuration surface and retain delivered outcome messages while relying on existing channel targeting to reduce visible prompts.

recommendation.title: Sponsor message and suppression now
recommendation.body: Accept a shared message|none contract with message as the upgrade-safe default, then track update mode separately behind generic delivery identifiers and channel edit capability.

likelyOwner.reason: Their active approval-lifecycle design proposal is the closest available evidence of ownership for the cross-channel contract decision.
